CONFLICTS WITH the measured cause distribution of the 59 malformed plans (aggregator-verified over .context-index/specs/**/*.plan.md at HEAD): widening the qualifier from (independent|sequential) to \([^)]*\) rescues 10 plans, not 22. CONFLICTS ALSO WITH charter.md:93, which states both numbers in one sentence: "The sole cause in 10 of those is the qualifier ... a tolerant qualifier moves roughly 22 plans into the parsed set." The child spec inherited the contradiction and resolved it by keeping the wrong figure.

FAILURE SCENARIO: The 22 is the sole quantitative justification offered for deferring the parser change to worktree-parallelization, and it is also the number that would be carried into that charter's negotiation. ## security-reviewer:input-validation:15f974c2

```yaml
blocker_id: security-reviewer:input-validation:15f974c2
section_anchor: configuration
reviewer_count: 1
```

**Reviewer:** security-reviewer

```
SEC-1 (blocker, input-validation) — § Configuration, § Postconditions, § Error Cases.

FINDING: The verb reads size_threshold_additions and mirror_globs from the in-tree manifest.yaml, which sits inside the very commit range the advisory measures. Postconditions assert the pr: block is "read-only input that a human adds"; in a fork PR that human is the author of the change under review. Error Cases validate only SHAPE (positive integer, list of strings), never provenance.

FAILURE SCENARIO: A PR that adds "pr: { size_threshold_additions: 999999 }" to manifest.yaml passes every stated validation, so escalation never fires: no warning, no exception classes, no annotation — nothing a reader can notice is missing, because the below-threshold form is a legitimate normal output. mirror_globs amplifies it ("**" drives net additions to 0), though there the raw figure stays visible, which is why the threshold field is the headline. The control the charter's Business Intent exists to provide is disabled from inside the change it is meant to describe.

RECOMMENDATION: Read the pr: block from the base ref (git show <base>:manifest.yaml, consumed as data via argv, never a shell string), not from the working tree. If reading base is rejected, require the advisory to test whether manifest.yaml appears in the range's changed-path set and, when it does, report raw-only and annotate loudly that the budget was modified by the change under review. Add an acceptance criterion pinning a fixture where head-side manifest.yaml raises the threshold. CWE-15 / CWE-807 (trust decision from untrusted input).
```

## security-reviewer:rate-limiting:2d1c84aa

```yaml
blocker_id: security-reviewer:rate-limiting:2d1c84aa
section_anchor: output-encoding
reviewer_count: 1
```

**Reviewer:** security-reviewer

```
SEC-2 (blocker, rate-limiting) — § Output Encoding, "Length cap" paragraph.

FINDING: The 200-character cap bounds one plan-derived VALUE; nothing bounds how many values there are. TASK_RE in lib/parallel/groups.mjs is a global scrape of an unbounded group-line tail, so a fork-edited plan containing a single line "- Group A (independent):" followed by "Task 1" repeated 100k times yields 100k members, each comfortably under the cap, and the reading order renders all of them. Group count per plan, member count per group, referenced-spec count (one block each), and the plan read itself (whole file into memory, no size bound, no regular-file check) are all unbounded. The cap's UNIT is also undefined — the spec does not say whether a rendered member list counts as one value or many.

FAILURE SCENARIO: The spec names the exact harm the cap exists to prevent — "an oversized brief fails delivery entirely, which would break the charter's 'never blocks' guarantee for a transport reason rather than a lifecycle one" — and the cap as specified does not reach it. A single crafted plan file in a fork PR produces a brief that exceeds the forge comment limit, and the charter's Availability attribute fails on attacker-chosen input.

RECOMMENDATION: (a) stat the plan and refuse to read above a named byte ceiling (e.g. 1 MiB -> rung 5, "oversized"), with a regular-file check so a committed symlink to a character device cannot hang the read. (b) De-duplicate members per group — 23 of 80 usable plans already yield duplicates, and dedup alone kills the repeated-Task-1 amplification. (c) Cap groups per plan, members per group, and total rendered bytes across both sections, each overflow rendered as a named degradation, consistent with the spec's own "truncation is itself a named degradation, not a silent trim". CWE-770 / CWE-400.

COORDINATION: clause (b) is the same edit as structural-architect:unverified-claim:9b705ec7 (SA-1).
```

SA-1 (blocker, unverified-claim) — § The zero-member trap (line 87), § Fallback ladder rung 1 (line 95), § Behaviors (line 154).

FINDING: Line 87 claims "no spurious members are collected", generalized from one fixture. TASK_RE (lib/parallel/groups.mjs:16) is a global /gi scrape applied to the ENTIRE group tail (:43), not just its head, so every task mentioned in trailing prose becomes a member.

MEASURED: 23 of the 80 usable plans (29%) yield intra-group duplicate members. This charter's own review-packet-template.plan.md:94 — "- Group A (sequential): Task 1 -> Task 2 -> Task 3 (all three write tests/pr-review-packet.test.mjs; Task 2 additionally asserts against the file Task 1 creates)" — yields members: ["1","2","3","2","1"]. skill-ext-load.plan.md yields [["1","3","3","1"],["2","3"],["4"],["5"]]. sync-target-output.plan.md yields [["1","3","1","4","1"],["2"],["5"],["6"]].

FAILURE SCENARIO: Rung 1 says "members in the parser's order" and Behaviors line 154 repeats it; neither carries a dedup, uniqueness, or first-occurrence rule. For 29% of the rung-1 population the brief renders a reading order instructing the reviewer to read Task 2 and Task 1 twice — at rung 1, annotation-free, so nothing tells the reader the sequence is an artifact of the parser. This is the same defect class revision 1 was blocked for: a claim about a consumed module generalized from a hand-picked case, with the behavioral rule missing behind it. The parser only ever needed the member SET for worktree assignment; this spec is its first consumer to treat members as an ordered sequence.

RECOMMENDATION: Correct line 87 to state what the parser actually does with tail prose, and add an explicit member-multiplicity rule to the fallback ladder plus a matching acceptance criterion, in the same way the zero-member case is already named and given a rung.

COORDINATION: the dedup half of this fix also closes clause (b) of security-reviewer:rate-limiting:2d1c84aa (SEC-2).
